alice (eng-runtime): Pushed a quick profiling summary — there are three hotspots affecting tail latency: kernel fallback on mixed-precision kernels, KV cache eviction churn for large contexts, and microbatching spikes when we hit batching timers. dashboard: <https://perf.redwood.internal/dash/serving/1710>
ben (sre): Can you paste the top-level numbers? p95/p99 across the 8-GPU pool?
alice (eng-runtime): p95 ~= 120ms, p99 ~= 420ms at 400rps steady-state (seq_len distribution: 512 median, 2048 5%). When we shift to microbatch size 8 -> throughput up but p99 jumps to ~700ms.
frank (perf): Kernel fallback is the killer on long seqs — the optimized attention kernel doesn't support the 2:1 KV-layout for this model, so it falls back to a slower path. That explains the p99 tail for the 5% 2048 requests.
carol (product): We're negotiating SLOs with a mid-market customer. They asked for p95 < 150ms and p99 < 300ms. Sales says they'd sign if p99 300 for their workload only. Is that realistic on hosted? :thinking:
david (sales): Customer workload has 95% seq_len 512, 5% 2048 bursts. They will pay for dedicated if needed but want a price estimate with those SLOs.
eva (solutions): For that distribution, a dedicated pool with pinned kernels + warmed KV cache should hit p95 120 and p99 ~280, assuming microbatching tuned to 4. Need to verify.
ben (sre): Important: KV cache eviction churn we saw this morning increases tail latencies massively when memory pressure causes TTL-based evictions. We need eviction metrics per-client to reason SLA.
frank (perf): I ran a trace. Attaching a snippet of the hot stack (p99 request):
```
0x7f13 kernel_select() at runtime/kernels.cc:412
0x7f22 dispatch_attention_fastpath() at runtime/attn.cc:88
0x7f33 protobuf_send() at runtime/net.cc:210
```
The kernel_select path takes 65% of the extra time for seq>=1024.
alice (eng-runtime): Two levers here: 1) change kernel selection to prefer the slower but predictable kernel for 2048 requests (makes p99 more stable); 2) isolate long-seq requests on a separate route/pool (reduce interference). Both have cost/throughput tradeoffs.
carol (product): For negotiation, product is comfortable accepting higher p95 if p99 is tighter or vice versa. We need a clear table: what combinations of (microbatch size, route isolation, kernel policy) yield p95/p99 numbers and cost delta.
david (sales): Customer will accept microbatching up to 8 to save cost, but not if it blows their p99. They asked for 30-day SLA window and a penalty ladder.
eva (solutions): My quick local sim: with microbatch=4, kernel_policy=prefer_predictable, route_isolation=true -> p95 130ms, p99 290ms, throughput down ~12%. If microbatch=8 throughput +20% but p99 hits 420ms.
frank (perf): Also note KV cache warm factor: cold-start for KV (first token after eviction) adds ~60ms. With per-customer pinned cache we can remove that.
ben (sre): Suggest adding a per-customer cache-warm metric and exposing percent-warm in the console. That will help sales/product decide on dedicated capacity.
alice (eng-runtime): Actionable proposal: for this customer, offer a dedicated pool with kernel pinning + microbatch=4 and an option to bump to microbatch=8 for cost-sensitive periods. Give them p95=140ms, p99=300ms SLA for dedicated. Need cost delta estimate from finance.
carol (product): That looks like a negotiable starting point. Product wants to know rollback strategy if we miss p99 — can we failover to a smaller model or drop to synchronous (single-request) mode?
alice (eng-runtime): Failover to a smaller model is doable (route -> fallback model) but increases semantic risk. Synchronous single-request mode will keep latency lower for tails but kills throughput. Prefer canary rollout + automatic fallback to next-best model if p99 exceeds threshold for 5 min.
david (sales): Customer also asked if we can provide p99 per-route and a one-week trial on dedicated before committing. We should agree on test harness and pass/fail criteria.
eva (solutions): We can give a trial with a preloaded workload and a dedicated pool. I can run a 48-hour soak and export p95/p99 histograms.
frank (perf): I'll produce a small runbook and perf graphs: microbatch sizes [1,2,4,8], kernel_policy [aggressive, predictable], route_isolation [on/off]. Will push results to the dashboard by EOD.
ben (sre): Also adding eviction metrics and a KV-warm % to the dashboard — PR incoming: #2742.
alice (eng-runtime): Quick config snippet for the dedicated pool we propose:
```yaml
pool: dedicated-cust-17
microbatch: 4
kernel_policy: prefer_predictable
route_isolation: true
kv_cache: pinned
SLOs:
  p95_ms: 140
  p99_ms: 300
```
david (sales): Perfect. Can you also include an estimated monthly cost delta vs hosted? I can present this next week.
frank (perf): Uploaded preliminary graphs here: <https://perf.redwood.internal/run/171070/graphs>. p95 lines look flat; p99 tails are the thing to watch.
carol (product): Next steps: frank runs the matrix + share numbers, ben wires eviction/KV metrics, eva schedules the 48h trial, finance to give cost delta. Product will draft the SLO language for the contract.
alice (eng-runtime): Agree. Tentative owners: frank (perf evidence), ben (ops dashboard), eva (trial), product (SLO text), sales (customer negotiation). I'll open a tracking ticket linking these. PRs: #2742 (kv metrics), #2750 (kernel-selection opt flags), #2751 (dedicated-pool templates).
